name: expiry-pill
title: Expiry pill
description: Shows a preview lifetime as fine, expiring soon, or expired. Does not verify codes, persist state, or grant or revoke access. Contract: the consumer owns lifecycle timestamps and action callbacks.

meta.whenToUse: A preview's remaining lifetime belongs next to the gate, or inside the bar that stays after unlock.
meta.notFor: Enforcing the deadline. The pill reaches its expired state and changes nothing about what your application serves.
pitfalls: Rendering the expired state hides nothing. Your own check decides whether the preview is still available.
`soonThreshold` is in seconds, not milliseconds. The default window is one hour.
meta.contract: Shows a preview lifetime as fine, expiring soon, or expired. Does not verify codes, persist state, or grant or revoke access. Contract: the consumer owns lifecycle timestamps and action callbacks.

props.name: expiresAt
props.description: Expiry timestamp as ISO 8601 with timezone; required.

props.name: soonThreshold
props.description: Duration considered expiring soon, in seconds.

props.name: labels
props.type: { pending?: string; fine?: string; soon?: string; expired?: string; unavailable?: string; remaining?: (seconds: number) => string; }

props.name: theme
props.description: Explicit theme; omitted follows the system preference.

meta.a11y: Native controls, visible focus, localized labels; lifecycle messages use polite announcements. No modal dialog is created.

docs: UI only. Read https://knock.codes/docs/expiry-pill.md. Consumers own authorization.
